2608.11977.title: Retry, Switch, or Abstain? Learning Strategy-Aware Tool-Use Policies via Controlled Error Injection
2608.11977.paper_summary: Tool-using LLM agents are commonly trained and evaluated in environments where tool calls succeed reliably, yet deployed tools can fail transiently, persistently, or silently. Robust recovery therefore requires more than repeated retries: an agent may need to retry the same path, switch to an alternative, or recognize that no viable path remains. We present BENCH2ROBUST, a framework that converts failure-free tool-use benchmarks into controlled stochastic environments with scenario-controlled solvability, where episodes explicitly require retrying, switching, or stopping after available paths are exhausted. We use BENCH2ROBUST to study two complementary interventions: structured runtime recovery context through Bayesian Tool Memory (BTM), and curriculum-controlled reinforcement learning. Across 7 models from 4 families and two multi-turn benchmark families, tool failures produce a near-universal robustness gap. On held-out Retail tasks, BTM improves robustness by up to 16.8 percentage points without retraining, while RL learns complementary recovery behavior that remains beneficial without inference-time BTM. Combining the two reaches 40.8-45.5% under injection while preserving failure-free performance. These results suggest that robust tool use benefits from combining environment-specific recovery knowledge with learned recovery behavior.
2608.11977.paper_summary_zh: 使用工具的 LLM 代理通常在工具調用可靠成功的環境中進行訓練和評估，但部署的工具可能會暫時、持久或靜默失敗。因此，穩健的恢復需要的不僅僅是重試：代理可能需要重試相同的路徑、切換到替代方案，或認識到沒有可行的路徑。 我們提出了 BENCH2ROBUST，一個將無失敗工具使用基準轉換為受控隨機環境的框架，這些環境具有場景控制的可解性，其中情節明確要求在可用路徑耗盡後進行重試、切換或停止。我們使用 BENCH2ROBUST 研究兩種互補的干預措施：通過貝葉斯工具記憶 (BTM) 的結構化運行時恢復上下文，以及課程控制的強化學習。在來自四個家族的七個模型和兩個多輪基準家族中，工具失敗產生了幾乎普遍的穩健性差距。在保留的零售任務上，BTM 在不重新訓練的情況下將穩健性提高了最多 16.8 個百分點，而 RL 學習的互補恢復行為在沒有推理時間 BTM 的情況下仍然有益。將兩者結合在注入下達到 40.8-45.5% 的效果，同時保持無失敗性能。這些結果表明，穩健的工具使用受益於將環境特定的恢復知識與學習到的恢復行為相結合。
